extracted text:
The paper describes the development of precipitation-strengthened aluminum alloys for non-quenchable aluminum metal matrix composites. The main alloys discussed are:

1. Al-0.09Sc-0.045Zr (at.%) (Alloy 1)
2. Al-0.06Sc-0.03Zr (at.%) (Alloy 2)

These alloys were cast from 99.99% pure Al and master alloys (Al-2Sc and Al-1.6Zr wt.%). The alloys were subjected to different cooling rates and a two-step aging treatment (300°C for 4h and 425°C for 8h).

The paper also discusses Al-Sc-Zr/Saffil composites with different volume fractions of Saffil (alumina) short fibers (0%, 4%, 15%).

For comparison, commercial alloys AA5083-H131 and AA6061-T6, as well as Al-2Cu/Saffil composites are mentioned.

The Al-2Cu wt.% contains 2% copper by weight.
property mapping:
- Microhardness: Reported in MPa in Table II
- Yield strength (YS): Reported in MPa in Table II
- Ultimate tensile strength (UTS): Reported in MPa in Tables II and III
- Elongation: Reported as percentage (%) in Tables II and III
- Toughness: Reported in MJ/m³ in Table III
- Alloy composition: Reported in both atomic percentage (at.%) and weight percentage (wt.%) in Table I
abbreviations:
- Al-Sc-Zr: Aluminum-Scandium-Zirconium alloy
- MMC: Metal Matrix Composite
- Al-MMC: Aluminum Metal Matrix Composite
- Saffil: High-purity crystalline alumina fibers (>96 vol.% Al₂O₃) with a small amount of silica (<4 vol.%)
- DCP-OES/DCP-AES: Direct Coupled Plasma-Optical Emission Spectroscopy/Atomic Emission Spectroscopy
- YS: Yield Strength
- UTS: Ultimate Tensile Strength
- at.%: Atomic percentage
- wt.%: Weight percentage
- vol.%: Volume percentage
